data.content_ref: inline:The target identifies the single best cross-city modulator as aridity/vegetation fraction via the latent heat pathway. However, empirical and theoretical UHI literature consistently finds that the cross-city variation in the nocturnal UHI intensity is primarily controlled by urban geometry (sky view factor / street canyon aspect ratio) and population/city size, not aridity or vegetation fraction. Notably, arid cities often exhibit much smaller nocturnal UHI than temperate/humid cities because urban irrigation and impervious cover can make the city cooler at night than the surrounding desert. Thus the selected single mechanism contradicts the observed behavior of arid cities.
